label: CHHATISGARH
reason: MoSPI spells the state with one t throughout the flash-report annexures (2009-10 to 2023-24); the Census-2011 and DataMeet spelling is Chhattisgarh, st_code 22. Same state, MoSPI house spelling — not a near match.

label: Orissa
reason: pre-2011 name. Renamed by the Orissa (Alteration of Name) Act 2011; Census st_code 21 is unchanged, and MoSPI kept printing the old name in the 2009-2012 annexures.

label: Uttaranchal
reason: pre-2007 name. Renamed by the Uttaranchal (Alteration of Name) Act 2006, effective 1 January 2007; Census st_code 5 is unchanged.

label: Jharkhandd
reason: a typo in MoSPI's own annexure — the state name with a doubled final d. Recorded as one explicit label rather than reached by similarity scoring.

label: A & N ISLANDS
reason: MoSPI's abbreviation of Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Needs an entry because the shared state normaliser drops the word 'Islands' as decoration, which leaves the two-letter 'a n' and matches nothing.

label: D & N HAVELI
reason: MoSPI's abbreviation of Dadra & Nagar Haveli. Since 2020 it is one UT with Daman & Diu but the two Census codes survive; 26 is the Dadra & Nagar Haveli side, matching the sansad:5536 decision already in data/india/pc-source-aliases.csv.

label: J & K
reason: MoSPI's abbreviation of Jammu & Kashmir. The shared normaliser turns it into 'j k', which matches nothing. Ladakh is st_code 38 and is never folded in here.

label: Himachal Pr.
reason: MoSPI abbreviates Pradesh to 'Pr.' in a handful of 2009-2011 rows.

label: Offshore
reason: not a place. MoSPI files offshore oil and gas projects (Mumbai High, the KG basin) under 'Offshore' because they sit outside every state's territory. st_code stays NULL, as it would if the label were unreadable — the difference this row records is that the source was precise and there is nothing left to resolve.

label: PAN India
reason: MoSPI's label for a project with no single location (telecom and pipeline networks). The whole country, so no single st_code — the same answer as 'Multi State', reached from a different word.
